title: Auth Control Plane authorization request (v1 wire format)
description:
One question put to the policy decision point: may this principal perform this action on this resource (TRD section 8, section 14: POST /v1/authorize). The caller is a policy-enforcement point (api, web, acr-api) asking; the answer is authorization_decision.v1.

A REQUEST CARRIES NO AUTHORITY. The principal is named by an opaque reference the decision point resolves server-side, never by roles, permissions, scopes or an organization the caller asserts (TRD section 2 principle 3: caller-supplied organization, resource, role, scope and actor values are requests or hints, never authority). So there is no `roles`, `permissions`, `scopes` or `is_superuser` member and `additionalProperties: false` is what makes that absence enforceable: a caller cannot add a claim the decision point might honour.

EVERY VOCABULARY IS CLOSED (ACP-ADR-05 decision 1, G-26: unknown action, resource, role, grant type, condition or entitlement key denies): the action uses principal.v1's action syntax by reference (a bare `admin` is invalid, G-27), `resource.type` is a closed set, and `context.client_service` is the inventory's closed service set by reference. The resource-type set below is the initial list; widening it is a deliberate schema amendment, and whether an action is REGISTERED and valid for a resource type is a decision-point check this schema cannot make.

Resource keys are canonical lowercase. A repository key is `owner/repo` or the explicit organization-wide `*` (TRD section 9); no other type may use `*`. `request_id` is the error.v1 shape by reference and, as everywhere in v1, is minted by the CALLER's own service for correlation and appears in the decision point's audit row, never echoed into a response.

schema_version.description: Identifies this document's contract. A relying party MUST reject an unrecognised value (G-26).

principal_reference.description: Opaque signed-or-internal reference the decision point resolves to a principal (TRD section 8). URL-safe characters only and bounded by the pattern alone (no redundant length keywords, which make validators report different keywords). A reference, never a credential value and never an identity claim: the decision point derives the principal.

action.description: The registered action asked about, e.g. acr.context.read. Same syntax as principal.v1 actions.

organization_id.description: Organization the resource belongs to, when it has one. Absent for platform-level resources. A hint for resolution, never authority: the decision point verifies it against the principal's memberships.

key.description: Canonical lowercase resource key. Its pattern depends on `type` (see the if/else below): `owner/repo` or `*` for a repository, a lowercase token for every other type.

client_service.description: The calling service, from the inventory's closed service set so the two cannot disagree on which services exist. The caller's identity is also established by its workload credential; this field is for metrics and audit labels (TRD section 19) and confers nothing.
